result.document_summary: New Jersey P.L. 2026, c.43, the Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act, which makes it an antitrust violation to use or operate algorithmic rent-setting coordination software for residential rentals.
result.notes: Effective date computed from section 9: first day of the twelfth month following enactment on July 20, 2026, i.e., 2027-07-01 (inferred from the text, not stated as a date). Section 6(b) bars conflicting municipal ordinances; it is recorded in the interaction field of the single algorithmic rent-setting rule. The act contains no rent-cap, eviction, deposit, fee or screening rules.

rules.title: FAIR Act: ban on algorithmic coordination of residential rental pricing
rules.requirement: It is an antitrust violation for a landlord to pay for or use a coordinator's services, for a coordinator to facilitate agreements restricting competition or to perform a coordinating function, or for anyone to engage in parallel pricing coordination or perform a coordinating function (e.g., algorithms that pool nonpublic data of multiple owners to set or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy). Public free rent estimates, research uses, equal-terms brokerage databases and government affordability controls are excluded.
rules.key_value: Unlawful to use or operate algorithmic rent-setting coordination software
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all rental property owners, coordinators and other persons dealing in residential dwelling units in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions_text: Excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care and detention or correctional facilities from 'residential dwelling units'; excludes research/testing uses, free public rent estimates, equal-terms brokerage listing databases, and government entities setting rents through affordability controls from 'coordinating function'/'coordinator'.
rules.interaction: Supplements and does not limit the New Jersey Antitrust Act (P.L.1970, c.73); section 6(b) prohibits municipalities from enacting ordinances that conflict with this act, except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law.
